discovery: Prediction and discovery of kilonovae, establishing neutron-star mergers as a cosmic site of r-process heavy-element nucleosynthesis

nominees.name: Daniel Kasen
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Ryan J. Foley
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Santa Cruz, USA

motivation: Where the heaviest elements such as gold and uranium are made was one of the great open questions in physics for sixty years. Metzger predicted that the radioactive decay of freshly synthesized r-process nuclei in neutron-star merger ejecta powers a distinct transient, the kilonova, and set its expected luminosity. Kasen showed through radiative-transfer calculations that lanthanide opacities make such emission red and long-lived, which gave observers a clear signature to look for. Foley led the team that made the first optical detection of the counterpart to the gravitational-wave event GW170817, and follow-up observations then matched the predicted kilonova, revealing roughly several Earth masses of freshly made heavy elements. This work connects nuclear physics, gravitational waves and the chemical record preserved in the oldest stars, such as single-event r-process enrichment in ancient dwarf galaxies. It turned speculation into direct observation.
